questions.q: Why is the learning rate usually fixed first, with the number of trees chosen by early stopping or cross-validation?
options: The two trade off: a smaller learning rate needs more trees, so they should be settled together
Learning rate has no effect on accuracy
Number of trees can only be set by hand
Early stopping only works at a learning rate of 1
questions.explain: A lower learning rate takes smaller steps and needs more trees. Fixing the rate and letting early stopping choose the count settles this pair first.

questions.q: What does min_child_weight control in XGBoost?
options: The learning rate of each tree
The number of features sampled per tree
The minimum amount of data weight a leaf must hold, which limits how finely trees can split
The maximum number of trees
questions.explain: Larger values make splits more conservative by requiring more data in each leaf, which helps prevent overfitting.

questions.q: In the lesson, the random search chose settings with a cross-validated AUC of 0.8344, yet the test AUC (0.826) did not beat the step-1 model (0.827). What is the best explanation?
options: The test set was used to tune the model
The best and worst trials scored within a narrow band that was smaller than fold-to-fold noise, so the winner was not reliably better
Random search never works
XGBoost ignores the settings given to it
questions.explain: All 25 trials scored between about 0.826 and 0.834 in CV, with a fold std near 0.009, so small gaps between trials were not meaningful.

questions.q: Which practice keeps the final test score honest while tuning?
options: Choose the settings that score best on the test set
Run the search separately on the test set as well
Tune on the full dataset, including the test rows
Tune only with cross-validation or a validation split on training data, and evaluate on the test set once at the end
questions.explain: If the test set guides tuning, its score becomes optimistically biased. Tune on training data and touch the test set once.

questions.q: Two settings score 0.8344 and 0.8338 in CV, and the fold-to-fold standard deviation is about 0.009. Which do you prefer?
options: The first, because it is higher
Whichever is simpler, because the gap is far smaller than the noise
Neither; discard both
The second, because lower is better
questions.explain: A 0.0006 gap against a 0.009 spread is a tie. When scores tie, prefer the simpler, more regularized model.
